name: Money
summary: Emergency cash, account access for a partner, beneficiaries, insurance review, credit freezes and tax records.
disclaimer: This is a checklist, not financial advice.
intro: What a household needs in place so that the money keeps working when something goes wrong: cash to hand, a partner who can reach the accounts, insurance that covers what you think it covers, and credit that nobody else can use.

items.done: Done when emergency cash in small bills is split between your bag and a second place at home.
Done when a card from a second bank or network is kept apart from your wallet, and you can enter its PIN from memory.

items.title: Keep an emergency savings fund in a separate account
items.done: Done when a savings account used only for emergencies exists, an automatic transfer into it runs at least monthly, and the target you have set for it is written on the bank and bills list.

items.title: Check that each bank and credit union you use is federally insured
items.done: Done when each institution is confirmed on the FDIC or NCUA lookup and no ownership category is over the insured limit.
Done when every automatic payment and regular bill is on the bank and bills list with its due day.

items.title: Decide what happens to the mail at a home left empty
items.done: Done when, for each home left empty for more than a few days, a neighbor collects the mail or the Postal Service is holding it (3 to 30 days), with a forwarding service for anything longer.

items.title: Have pay and government benefits paid by direct deposit
items.done: Done when no regular income or benefit arrives as a paper check by mail.
Done when every bank, card and loan is on the bank and bills list with its phone number and no passwords.
Done when email, banking and cloud storage each have a unique password and multi-factor sign-in.

items.title: Check how each account is owned and who receives it if an owner dies
items.done: Done when the beneficiary and account owner check has a row for every account showing how it is owned, confirmed with the bank.

items.title: Name a trusted contact on investment accounts and an emergency contact at your bank
items.done: Done when each brokerage account lists a trusted contact person and each bank that offers it has an emergency contact on file.

items.title: Make sure each adult can pay the essential bills alone, with no shared password
items.done: Done when each adult has, within the last 12 months, paid each essential bill alone, from an account in their own name or through access the bank itself granted them, without using anyone else's password, because federal rules do not count a transfer as unauthorized when you gave that person the means to reach your account, until you tell the bank otherwise.

items.title: Check the beneficiary on every retirement plan and IRA
items.done: Done when you have confirmed the named primary and backup beneficiaries on each workplace plan and IRA against its latest statement or the plan's records.

items.title: Check the beneficiary on every life insurance policy, including coverage through work
items.done: Done when each life policy, private or through an employer, has the beneficiaries you intend on the insurer's or plan's records.

items.title: Recheck beneficiaries and account owners after a marriage, divorce, birth or death
items.done: Done when the beneficiary and account owner check carries the date of your last check and every change since the last life event has been sent to the plan, insurer or bank.
Done when every policy you hold is on the insurance and legal list with its claims phone number.
Done when your contents limit, living-elsewhere limit and main exclusions are written on the insurance and legal list.
Done when you have looked up your address on FEMA's flood map and either hold a flood policy or have a quote in hand and your written reason for declining it on the insurance and legal list.
Done when a room-by-room video and the belongings catalog are saved away from home.

items.title: Ask your insurer how it treats a home left empty
items.done: Done when, for each home that stands empty for weeks at a time, your insurer has told you how long it may stand empty or unoccupied before coverage changes and whether an endorsement keeps it covered, and the answer is on the insurance and legal list.

items.title: Check the address where each car is kept on its policy
items.done: Done when each car's declarations page shows the address where the car is mostly kept, and you tell your insurer whenever that changes.
Done when a note reading “photograph damage, keep receipts, log every call” is clipped to the insurance and legal list.

items.title: If you own your home, check the policy would rebuild it and pay for living elsewhere
items.done: Done when the insurance and legal list shows, for each home you own, the dwelling limit beside today's rebuilding cost, whether the policy pays replacement cost or actual cash value, and the limit for additional living expenses.

items.title: Ask which common exclusions your home or renters policy has, such as sewer backup or earthquake
items.done: Done when the insurance and legal list has, for each home, a yes or no for each of sewer backup, earthquake and flood, and you have asked your insurer for a quote on each “no” that applies to you.

items.title: Check whether your car policy covers flood, fire and falling objects
items.done: Done when the insurance and legal list shows, for each vehicle, whether it has comprehensive coverage and what its deductible is.

items.title: Find out what life and disability coverage each earner has, including through work
items.done: Done when the insurance and legal list shows, for each earner, any life and disability coverage and whether it ends if they leave the job.

items.title: Check your liability limits and ask whether an umbrella policy is offered
items.done: Done when the liability limits on your home and car policies are written on the insurance and legal list, with your insurer's answer on umbrella coverage.
Done when each card issuer's lost-card number is on the bank and bills list, with the web address for placing a fraud alert.
Done when every adult has read the warning signs once and the household has agreed one rule: nobody pays or gives details to anyone who contacted you first.

items.title: Freeze your credit at all three national credit bureaus
items.done: Done when each adult has a freeze in place at Equifax, Experian and TransUnion and knows how to lift it.

items.title: Freeze the credit of each child under 16
items.done: Done when each child under 16 has a freeze at all three bureaus.

items.title: Check your credit reports from all three bureaus
items.done: Done when each adult has read a report from each bureau through AnnualCreditReport.com within the last 12 months.

items.title: Save your state's consumer protection number to report price gouging and repair fraud
items.done: Done when your state consumer protection or attorney general complaint line is in every adult's phone and on the paper contact list.

items.title: Keep your tax returns and records, with a copy stored away from home
items.done: Done when recent returns and their supporting records are kept for the IRS time limits, with a scanned backup outside the home.

items.title: Get an IRS Identity Protection PIN for each person in the household
items.done: Done when each person with a Social Security number or ITIN is enrolled and you know you must collect a new PIN each year.

items.title: Set up an IRS online account for each adult
items.done: Done when each adult who files can sign in to an IRS online account.

items.title: If your household keeps homes in more than one state, ask which state each adult is domiciled in
items.done: Done when a tax preparer or the state revenue department has told each adult which state is their domicile for income tax, and the answer is kept with your tax records.

items.title: Know where to check IRS disaster relief and how to get copies of past returns
items.done: Done when the IRS disaster relief page is bookmarked and each adult has signed in to their IRS online account once.
